inScope: lifraen-efnafraedi — PREVIEW ONLY (17 of 342 source modules — those with extracted segments already present in 02-for-mt/)

method: Counted by PARSING with @xmldom/xmldom — never by regex over raw XML, per this repo's standing rule. Two independent counting units are reported for every number, and must not be conflated:

countingUnits.rawMediaAltCensus: the number of <media> elements (any nesting depth) carrying a non-empty `alt` (mediaAttrs.alt || the child <image>/<iframe>'s alt), found by parsing each module's <content> with @xmldom/xmldom and reading getAttribute('alt'). This is the design spec's own census method (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-15-figure-alt-into-pipeline-design.md §1) and is a physical count of source material — it does not know or care what the extractor currently does with each element. UNCHANGED by Task 10 (it counts source bytes, not extractor behaviour).
countingUnits.emittedAltSegments: the number of 'alt'-typed segments actually produced by tools/cnxml-extract.js's extractSegments(), called in-memory on this branch (feat/c81-figure-alt) — no CLI run, per the global constraint. This is what the pipeline currently outputs. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-15 after Task 10's fix — every number under this key in this file is the POST-FIX value.

task10Fix.trigger: [LEAD] ruling, added after Task 9: fix the duplicate alt segment ids before the whole-branch review. Task 9 had measured 5 duplicate alt segment ids in chemistry and 16 duplicate alt-text emissions in organic (4 of which fall inside the 17-module in-scope preview), across 14 real modules, verified NEW to this branch (0 at pre-branch commit 40d0f0d4).
task10Fix.briefsProposedFixWasEmpiricallyFalsified: The task brief located a root cause and prescribed an exact fix: strip <para> from the string scanned for standalone <media> in processTopLevelContent (tools/cnxml-extract.js), on the theory that a bare top-level <media> nested directly in a <para> gets extracted twice. Applied VERBATIM as a standalone change and re-measured against the two named affected modules (m68739.cnxml, m68764.cnxml): the duplicate counts were BYTE-IDENTICAL before and after (956/104 total, 5/4 duplicates, unchanged). The brief's diagnosis describes a real defect, but not the one firing in the actual corpus — verified by reading both modules' source: m68739's duplicate is a <list> nested in a <para> that is a direct child of <example> (not a bare <media> in a top-level <para>); m68764's duplicate is a <figure> nested in a <para> that is a direct child of <problem> inside an <exercise> (again, not the brief's shape — and figures are extracted by an unconditional GLOBAL scan in processTopLevelContent that the brief's para-strip, scoped only to the standalone-media scan, does not touch). This falsification is the reason the fix below has two parts, not one.

actualFixTwoParts.part1_processTopLevelContent_paraStrip: Applied as originally prescribed (the brief's diagnosis, while not the cause of the two Task-9-named real corpus duplicates, is a genuine defect: a bare top-level <media>, no figure/list wrapper, direct child of a top-level <para>). Strips <para> from the string scanned for standalone <media>, mirroring the container-strip idiom already applied to example/exercise/note/figure/table/list. Measured corpus-inert across the 166 IN-SCOPE modules (chemistry 149 + organic preview 17) — this specific shape occurs in 0 of them, so within the deliverable's scope this part alone is a regression guard for the two synthetic fixtures in cnxml-extract-alt.test.js that were written to pin the old bug, not an active fix. ⚠️ It IS reachable, and DOES fire, in the broader out-of-scope 342-module organic corpus — confirmed directly: m00018.cnxml, m00078.cnxml, and m00330.cnxml each had 1–2 bogus top-level `type:'media'` structure entries removed by this part (verified via structure.content diff: e.g. m00018's top-level types went from ['media','para','figure',...] to ['para','figure',...]), and m00230.cnxml had the same shape one level down, inside a <section>. Every removed entry was a genuine duplicate of a media element already correctly rendered inline within its own paragraph — confirmed by image-src count in the rendered output going from 2 to 1, never to 0. Do not generalise the '0 of 166' finding to the full 342-module population.
actualFixTwoParts.part2_extractInlineText_ownershipSuppres: SUPERSEDED 2026-08-15 (review round 2) — see reviewRound2CriticalRegression below. This described the ORIGINAL Part 2, which suppressed altText at capture time based on a structural 'ownership' guess. That guess caused a critical regression and was replaced; kept here only as a historical record of what review round 2 found and fixed. Original text: In extractInlineText's inline-<media> capture, a <media> match was checked against the <figure> and <list> spans present WITHIN THE SAME TEXT being flattened, and when it fell inside one of those spans its inlineMediaMap entry was stored with altText suppressed to ''.

task10Fix.part2_reworked_dedupeAltSegments: REPLACES the original Part 2 (review round 2, 2026-08-15). Both structural walks now create their OWN alt segment normally, exactly as they did before Task 10 existed — nothing is suppressed at capture time. A NEW function, dedupeAltSegments(), runs ONCE at the end of extractSegments(), AFTER structure.content and structure.inlineMedia both exist, and MERGES true duplicates: (1) literal id collisions — provably safe, since altElementId() is deterministic from the media's own id, so two alt segments sharing one id can only mean the same id-bearing <media> was captured twice; (2) identical alt TEXT where at least one side is a positionally-numbered (id-less-media) alt id — id-less media's two capture paths never collide on id, so text is the only signal, and requiring only ONE side positional (not both) is necessary because processFigure anchors an id-less media's alt on `mediaAttrs.id || figure.id`, so a figure with its OWN id produces a NON-positional id (e.g. `fig-00006-alt`) for the SAME duplicate whose OTHER copy is positional (`media-N-alt`) — an asymmetry that caused a real test failure in this rework and was fixed by relaxing 'both positional' to 'either positional'. For every removed duplicate, every structural reference that pointed at it (a figure's `media.alt`, a standalone `media` node's `alt`, an `inlineMedia[]` entry's `alt`) is repointed to the survivor's segment id — whichever copy cnxml-inject.js actually renders, it now resolves to the SAME translated segment. This design is deliberately agnostic to WHICH copy the injector renders (see reviewRound2CriticalRegression — that was exactly the wrong question to ask).

reviewRound2CriticalRegression.whatWasFound: The whole-branch reviewer traced buildCnxml() output (not just extraction-side segments) and found 14 alt attributes lost entirely across 5 modules outside the 14 this branch's own tests covered: edlisfraedi-2e m42296 (23→19), m42714 (11→7), m42359 (19→18), m42493 (8→6); liffraedi-2e/ch29/m66590 (8→5). The <media>/<image> elements survived, stripped of alt — worse than the English-alt defect this task exists to fix, and structurally invisible to every extraction-side test because structure.inlineMedia entries carried no `alt` key at all (readAlt(undefined) is falsy, so buildMediaElement never writes the attribute regardless of the segment map).
reviewRound2CriticalRegression.rootCause: The original Part 2 suppressed the DATA on whichever copy looked 'structurally redundant' (nested inside a <figure>/<list>) at CAPTURE time, on the assumption that the OTHER (figure/list-owned) copy is what renders. That assumption is false for real shapes: cnxml-inject.js's exercise/note DOM builders (buildExerciseDom, buildNoteDom) FLATTEN a <list> nested in a <para> into the enclosing para and render THAT copy — exactly the one being suppressed — while the separately-built processList segment sits on a rendering path buildCnxml never reaches for that shape. Chemistry and organic's originally-checked 14 modules escaped only because their duplicate <media> happened to ALSO be caught by a pre-existing, id-based dedup regex in cnxml-inject.js (deduplicateMedia / the figure-in-para strip) — which is why the 14-module check read clean and the regression was invisible until the render consumer was traced on a wider population.
reviewRound2CriticalRegression.fix: Reworked Part 2 to never suppress data — see part2_reworked_dedupeAltSegments above. The question 'which structural walk owns this' was the wrong question; the right one is 'which copy does the injector render', and that is unknowable in general at capture time. Merging AFTER both copies exist, and repointing every reference, sidesteps the question entirely.
reviewRound2CriticalRegression.importantFinding_m66449_multiSubfigureFi: A SEPARATE, genuine content-loss finding (not a duplicate — a true drop): liffraedi-2e/ch04/m66449.cnxml, figure fig-ch04-03-01, a <figure> with two <subfigure>-wrapped <media> children inside a <para> inside a <note>. processFigure's own media-matching regex is non-global (figure.content.match(/<media[^>]*>…/), no /g flag) and only ever reaches the FIRST <media> — the second subfigure's alt has no processFigure emitter regardless of Task 10. Under the ORIGINAL (suppress-based) Part 2, BOTH subfigures' inline captures were suppressed as 'figure-owned', but only the first had an actual owner (processFigure) — the second lost its alt entirely. Measured corpus-wide by two independent instruments: exactly one such loss across all 1,192 modules. STATUS: FIXED, not deferred — and fixed FOR FREE by the rework, with no processFigure change needed: since neither capture is suppressed anymore, subfigure 1's inline capture merges with processFigure's emission (literal id collision, Rule 1), and subfigure 2's inline capture has no duplicate anywhere in the module, so neither merge rule touches it and it survives as its own segment. Verified directly: extracting m66449.cnxml now yields exactly 2 alt segments, one per subfigure, both with real text; the injected round-trip shows rawAlt=11=outAlt=11 (full parity, zero loss anywhere in the module). A dedicated regression test reproduces this exact shape (tools/__tests__/cnxml-extract-alt.test.js, describe('§C81 Task 10 review round 2 — duplicate alt data is never lost, only merged')).

task10Fix.part3_renderInjectSideFix_tools_cnxml_in: UNCHANGED by the review-round-2 rework, and still necessary — the \s→\b widening in buildExampleDom/buildExerciseDom/buildNoteDom's media-strip regexes remains correct and load-bearing: it is what lets the injector's pre-existing dedup mechanisms recognize and strip a duplicate <media> reconstructed with fewer attributes than before (e.g. organic's id-less media, which after dedupeAltSegments's merge may carry the SAME resolved alt as its figure-owned sibling but is still a distinct DOM occurrence that needs stripping to avoid rendering twice). Root cause, mechanism, and verification are as originally recorded: buildExampleDom/buildExerciseDom/buildNoteDom each strip an already-figure-owned <media> reconstructed inline in a para's text via a regex that required \s (at least one attribute) after '<media' — widened to \b (a word boundary, matching both '<media>' and '<media id="x">') at all three sites. A dedicated regression test (tools/__tests__/cnxml-inject.test.js, 'strips a ZERO-ATTRIBUTE expanded <media> too') is confirmed to fail against the old \s regex and pass against the new \b regex.

duplicateAltSegmentIds.historicalMechanism: m68739.cnxml: a <list> nested inside a <para> that is a direct child of <example> was processed twice — once via the para's own flattened inline text (extractInlineText + drainInlineMediaAlts), and again via processExample's separate extractNestedElements(example.content,'list') + processList() walk over the same list, which (unlike emitExerciseSection's orderedExerciseBlocks) did not exclude a list already reached through its enclosing para. m68764.cnxml: a <figure> nested inside a <para> that is a direct child of <problem> was processed twice — once via global figure extraction (extractNestedElements(content,'figure') → processFigure, which runs regardless of nesting depth or container), and again because the enclosing para's own inline-media regex matched the media even though it sits inside a nested <figure>. Both mechanisms are now closed by extractInlineText suppressing the alt of any <media> it finds nested inside a <figure> or <list> within the text it is flattening — see task10Fix.actualFixTwoParts.part2 above.

The 443-count gap (was 422 pre-fix — widened by exactly 21, the number of duplicate emissions removed, since those duplicates had been artificially inflating emittedAltSegmentsTotal and masking part of the true gap) is fully explained by TWO mechanisms, one no longer contributing: 442 alt-bearing <media> elements across the 491-module corpus sit in FOUR structural positions the current extractor cannot reach at all (table-entry-and-not-figure cells: 274 = 29 chem + 245 organic; bare media with <example> as direct parent: 105, chem only; bare media directly in <problem>/<solution>: 53, chem only; bare media with <note> as direct parent: 10, chem only — UNCHANGED, pre-existing, orthogonal to §C81), plus one regex-truncation drop in the opposite direction (−1, chem, m68727 — UNCHANGED, out of scope). The double-extraction mechanism that used to partially offset the gap (+21) is FIXED as of 2026-08-15 (Task 10) and now contributes 0. Arithmetic: 442 (unreachable) − 0 (double-extraction, fixed) + 1 (regex-truncation drop) = 443 — EXACT match to the measured gap, no unexplained residual.

candidateExplanationsChecked.mediaReachedByTwoPathsOrSkippedContainer: CONFIRMED as Task 9's finding, and FIXED 2026-08-15 (Task 10, [LEAD]-ruled, before the whole-branch review). Task 9 measured +21 across the 491-module corpus (5 chemistry + 16 organic-full, 4 of the 16 inside the in-scope preview), fired on 14 real modules, and traced it to a stale restatement of Task 3's own correct-at-its-vintage '0 of 491'. Task 10 verified the brief's proposed root cause (processTopLevelContent not stripping <para> before its standalone-media scan) does NOT match the actual corpus mechanism — applying it verbatim produced a byte-identical measurement, empirically falsifying the diagnosis for the real duplicates (though it remains a valid fix for a different, corpus-inert synthetic shape, kept as a regression guard). The REAL mechanisms — a <list> nested in a <para> inside <example> (processExample's own separate list re-walk not excluding lists already reached through their enclosing para), and a <figure> nested in a <para> anywhere (global, unconditional figure extraction combined with extractInlineText's inline-media match not knowing to skip content already owned by a nested <figure>) — are fixed by making extractInlineText suppress the alt of any <media> it finds nested inside a <figure> or <list> within the text it is flattening, since both container types are always independently reached by a dedicated structural walk. See task10Fix above for full detail, verification method, and the acceptance test.

schemaNote: Field/key shapes deliberately diverge from the brief's illustrative Step-1 script (which used a flat `altSegments` count and the bare book slug as key): `emittedAltSegments.total` vs `rawMediaAltCensus.total` are kept as separate, clearly-named siblings because the two counting units must never be read as interchangeable (see countingUnits above) — a flat `altSegments` field would silently pick one and hide the other. `lifraen-efnafraedi_preview` (vs bare `lifraen-efnafraedi`) is used as the book key specifically so it sits alongside `lifraen-efnafraedi_FULL_342_modules_NOT_in_scope` under fullCorpusReconciliation without a naming collision. The top-level `task10Fix` key is new (2026-08-15) and documents the fix, its empirical-falsification finding, and its verification method in one place, so a reader does not have to reconstruct that narrative from scattered per-book notes. Nothing currently reads this file programmatically; §C82 (named as its eventual consumer in the plan) should either adopt this shape or this file should be adapted to whatever shape §C82 needs.
